    <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock contextRef="C_0000087347_20210101_20210630" id="F_000437">
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;8.&#160;&#160; &lt;span style="text-decoration:underline;"&gt;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over 120 countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; &lt;/span&gt;Amounts recorded in&lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt; Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss &lt;/span&gt;are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks.&#160;&#160;Included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Assets&lt;/span&gt; was $309 million at June 30, 2021 ($427 million at December 31, 2020) and included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Liabilities&lt;/span&gt; was $56 million at June 30, 2021 ($13 million at December 31, 2020) relating to the fair value of outstanding cross-currency swap derivatives.&#160;&#160;The fair value was determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;1.5 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;1.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.00% Notes due 2024, &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.29%, 2.51% and 2.76%, respectively.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the first quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;0.8 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;0.8 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 1.87% and 2.20%, respectively. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;2.0 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;2.0 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;2032.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the swapped portion of the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;2.77&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;% and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;3.49&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;%, respectively.&#160; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the third quarter of 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $0.5 billion of US dollar denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of $0.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its $0.5 billion 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of 1.73%.&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and changes in the fair value are recognized in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss), &lt;/span&gt;as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;At June 30, 2021, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $8.5 billion in various foreign currencies, of which $6.2 billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Other than the previously mentioned cross-currency swaps, the fair value of the other outstanding derivatives was not material at June 30, 2021 and December 31, 2020. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The effect of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, and those not designated as hedges, on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss) &lt;/span&gt;was as follows: &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $69 million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments &amp;amp; other&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)&lt;/span&gt;.&#160; See Note 2 &#x2013; &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Charges and Credits&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsDisclosureTextBlock>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11,230</p></td>
<td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:double 2.5pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First quarter 2020:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were </span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top"/>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> that resulted in a $</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">3.1</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> billion goodwill impairment charge</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results. The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between 12.0% and 13.5%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a 50-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the seven reporting units, on average, by less than 5%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">As previously noted, late in the first quarter of 2020, geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time as demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to a collapse in oil prices.&#160;&#160;As a result, the second quarter of 2020 was the most challenging quarter in decades.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger responded to these market conditions by taking actions to restructure its business and rationalize its asset base during the second quarter of 2020.&#160;&#160;These actions included reducing headcount, closing facilities and exiting business lines in certain countries.&#160;&#160;Additionally, due to the resulting activity decline, Schlumberger had assets that would no longer be utilized.&#160;&#160;As a consequence of these circumstances and decisions, Schlumberger recorded the following restructuring and asset impairment charges:</span></p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The estimated fair value of Schlumberger&#8217;s <span style="font-style:italic;">Long-term Debt, </span>based on quoted market prices at June 30, 2021 and December 31, 2020, was $16.7 billion and $17.3 billion, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2021, Schlumberger replaced its &#8364;1.54 billion one-year committed facility with a &#8364;750 million <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000757">three-year</span> committed revolving credit facility maturing in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000758">June 2024</span>.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2021 no amounts had been drawn under this facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to the revolving credit facility described above, at June 30, 2021, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $5.75 billion with commercial banks, of which $5.56 billion was available and unused. &#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $2.75 billion matures in February 2023, $2.0 billion matures in February 2025 and $1.0 billion matures in July 2026.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at June 30, 2021 and December 31, 2020 were $0.2 billion and $0.4 billion, respectively, all of which&#160;was classified in&#160;<span style="font-style:italic;">Long-term debt</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance </span><span style="color:#000000;">Sheet</span>.&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span>  </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2021, Schlumberger repurchased all $665 million of its 3.30% Senior Notes due 2021.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#8364;400 million of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#8364;400 million of 0.50% Notes due 2031.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#8364;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026, $900 million of 2.65% Senior Notes due 2030 and &#8364;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger repurchased all $600 million of its 4.20% Senior Notes due 2021 and $935 million of its 3.30% Senior Notes due 2021.&#160; Schlumberger paid a premium of approximately $40 million in connection with these repurchases.&#160; This premium was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &amp; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; <span style="font-style:italic;">Charges and Credits</span>.<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger established a &#8364;5.0 billion Guaranteed Euro Medium Term Note program that provides for the issuance of various types of debt instruments such as fixed or floating rate notes in euro, US dollar or other currencies.&#160; Schlumberger has not issued any debt under this program.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger Limited fully and unconditionally guarantees the securities issued by certain of its subsidiaries, including securities issued by Schlumberger Investment SA and Schlumberger Finance Canada Ltd., both wholly-owned subsidiaries of Schlumberger.</p><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2021</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureAbstract', window );"><strong>Derivative Instruments And Hedging Activities Disclosure [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</a></td>
<td class="text">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over 120 countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks.&#160;&#160;Included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Other Assets</span> was $309 million at June 30, 2021 ($427 million at December 31, 2020) and included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Other Liabilities</span> was $56 million at June 30, 2021 ($13 million at December 31, 2020) relating to the fair value of outstanding cross-currency swap derivatives.&#160;&#160;The fair value was determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;1.5 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;1.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;0.5 billion 0.00% Notes due 2024, &#8364;0.5 billion 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#8364;0.5 billion 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.29%, 2.51% and 2.76%, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;0.8 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;0.8 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;0.4 billion of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#8364;0.4 billion of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 1.87% and 2.20%, respectively. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;2.0 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;2.0 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#8364;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2032.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the swapped portion of the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2.77</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">% and </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3.49</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">%, respectively.&#160; </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the third quarter of 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $0.5 billion of US dollar denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of $0.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its $0.5 billion 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of 1.73%.<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and changes in the fair value are recognized in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss), </span>as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At June 30, 2021, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $8.5 billion in various foreign currencies, of which $6.2 billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other than the previously mentioned cross-currency swaps, the fair value of the other outstanding derivatives was not material at June 30, 2021 and December 31, 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effect of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, and those not designated as hedges, on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss) </span>was as follows: </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for loss and gain contingencies. Describes any existing condition, situation, or set of circumstances involving uncertainty as of the balance sheet date (or prior to issuance of the financial statements) as to a probable or reasonably possible loss incurred by an entity that will ultimately be resolved when one or more future events occur or fail to occur, and typically discloses the amount of loss recorded or a range of possible loss, or an assertion that no reasonable estimate can be made.</p></div>
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">+ References</a><div style="display: none;"><p>Reference 1: http://fasb.org/us-gaap/role/ref/legacyRef<br> -Publisher FASB<br> -Name Accounting Standards Codification<br> -Topic 450<br> -SubTopic 30<br> -URI http://asc.fasb.org/subtopic&amp;trid=2127197<br><br>Reference 2: http://fasb.org/us-gaap/role/ref/legacyRef<br> -Publisher FASB<br> -Name Accounting Standards Codification<br> -Topic 450<br> -SubTopic 20<br> -URI http://asc.fasb.org/subtopic&amp;trid=2127163<br></p></div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for reporting segments including data and tables. Reportable segments include those that meet any of the following quantitative thresholds a) it's reported revenue, including sales to external customers and intersegment sales or transfers is 10 percent or more of the combined revenue, internal and external, of all operating segments b) the absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10 percent or more of the greater, in absolute amount of 1) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss or 2) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that did report a loss c) its assets are 10 percent or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.</p></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $69 million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &amp; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; <span style="font-style:italic;">Charges and Credits</span>.</p><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount after unamortized (discount) premium and debt issuance costs of long-term debt classified as noncurrent and excluding amounts to be repaid within one year or the normal operating cycle, if longer.
